title: Common admissible scalar from compact ultrametric balls
statement:
Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a multiplicative absolute value $|\cdot|:K\to\mathbf R_{\geq0}$ satisfying $|a|=0\iff a=0$, $|1|=1$, $|ab|=|a||b|$, and $|a+b|\leq\max(|a|,|b|)$. Let $V$ be a $K$-vector space with a norm $\|\cdot\|:V\to\mathbf R_{\geq0}$ satisfying $\|v\|=0\iff v=0$, $\|av\|=|a|\|v\|$, and $\|v+w\|\leq\max(\|v\|,\|w\|)$. A $K$-linear map means an additive map preserving multiplication by scalars. Assume that every closed ball $\{b\in K:|b-a|\leq r\}$, for $a\in K$ and real $r\geq0$, is compact for the metric $d(a,b)=|a-b|$ (every open cover admits a finite subcover). For every $K$-linear subspace $U\subseteq V$, every $K$-linear map $g:U\to K$ with $|g(u)|\leq\|u\|$ for all $u\in U$, and every $x\in V\setminus U$, there exists $b\in K$ such that
$$|b-g(u)|\leq\|x-u\|\qquad\text{for every }u\in U.$$
No closedness or finite dimension of $U$, and no completeness of $V$, is assumed.

proof.text: Use the existing NormedField and NormedAddCommGroup metrics, with distance equal to the norm of the difference. Mathlib supplies norm symmetry and closedness of metric closed balls. Linearity gives g(u)-g(w)=g(u-w).

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of compact admissible-ball selection: elementary argument, step 1.

proof.text:
For $u\in U$ put $c_u=g(u)$, $r_u=\|x-u\|$ and $B_u=\{b\in K:|b-c_u|\leq r_u\}$. All $r_u$ are nonnegative, and $c_u\in B_u$. Since $u-v=(u-x)+(x-v)$ and $u-v\in U$, the assumed bound and step 1 give
$$|c_u-c_v|=|g(u-v)|\leq\|u-v\|\leq\max(r_u,r_v).$$

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of compact admissible-ball selection: elementary argument, step 2.

proof.text: If r_u <= r_w and b belongs to B_u, write b-g(w)=(b-g(u))+(g(u)-g(w)). The scalar ultrametric inequality and step 2 show |b-g(w)| <= r_w, so B_u is a subset of B_w. Totality of the real order therefore makes the nonempty family (B_u), indexed by U, directed under reverse inclusion: for any two indices take the one with smaller radius. This packages the finite-minimum argument of the original proof.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of compact admissible-ball selection: elementary argument, step 3.

proof.text: Each B_u is a metric closed ball and hence closed by Mathlib Metric.isClosed_closedBall. Its radius is a norm, hence nonnegative. Its center g(u) belongs to B_u, so each B_u is nonempty. The hypothesis hcompact makes each B_u compact, including when the radius is zero.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of compact admissible-ball selection: elementary argument, step 4.

proof.text: Apply the directed-family form of the compact closed finite-intersection principle [lem-sfb-compact-closed-finite-intersection], implemented in Mathlib by IsCompact.nonempty_iInter_of_directed_nonempty_isCompact_isClosed. The index type U is nonempty because it contains zero; step 3 gives directedness and step 4 gives nonemptiness, compactness and closedness of every ball. Thus there is b in every B_u. Rewriting closed-ball membership as norm(b-g(u)) <= norm(x-u) gives the desired scalar. This is the same finite-intersection argument, with its finite-family induction and restriction to a fixed compact ball performed by Mathlib.
